#3548. You can expect a similar leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 as there is between GTA 5 and GTA 6, CD Projekt Red says

CD Projekt Red has said people can expect a similar qualitative and technological leap from The Witcher 3 to The Witcher 4 as has been witnessed between Grand Theft Auto 5 and Grand Theft Auto 6.

CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski made the remark during a Q3 earnings call this afternoon, during which he and CDPR faced a handful of questions related to GTA 6.

"First of all, obviously this is a call about us, not about Rockstar," Nowakowski began by saying, "but I do understand the connection here. Having said that, I'm not going to make a deep-dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course we did look at the game, we did see the differences.

"We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 - I think so, yes. It's been 11 years, we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."

Another question was about whether GTA 6 had affected development plans for The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 - a question well-timed after Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski joked at the weekend that "Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled" because of how impressive GTA 6 is.

"Is seeing GTA 6 launch making us make the games more expensive?" said Nowakowski. "We have certain ambitions when it comes to Witcher [4] and Cyberpunk 2; they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6. If anything happened as a result of GTA 6, it's [that it's] always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done, and that's for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers."

Specifically in terms of budget, Nowakowski said nothing had changed, and also echoed a point made earlier this year when he said Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 are "not budget-driven developments".

"I'm not saying we don't care about the budgets: we do, and I'm pretty sure [Rockstar] did as well. But you cannot make games like that having in mind 'this is the fixed number of money I want to spend and that's it, otherwise I'm gone'," he said.

"They're ambition-driven developments and money's important - the budgets are not indefinite, that's not what we're saying. But the philosophy is like I said, and honestly that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6's release; it has just always been like that."

When asked whether the arrival of GTA 6 had impacted sales of The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077, Nowakowski answered "yes and no". "You do see a certain dip in engagement on the PlayStation and Xbox for sure," he said.

Statistics apparently show a drop of "at least" 25 percent in CDPR's players as they "engaged themselves with GTA 6". "But you do have to remember that a lot of our players are PC-based," Nowakowski pointed out. "GTA has not launched on PC; we have not seen any impact whatsoever on the PC sales or engagement. So it's a bit of a mixed answer.

"And also on the PS5 and Xbox, it's not like our sales came to zero," he added. "Some short impact, yes, on the consoles. Long-term, we do not really see that affecting ourselves in any material way in Q4."

Finally, the questioning turned to marketing, which Rockstar has shown can reach far and wide if you have the brand-power of GTA and some imagination. We've seen prestigious department stores like Selfridges taken over by Rockstar for GTA 6, trailers premiering on Netflix, Miami launch festivals - Rockstar's marketing department has gone all out.

CDPR is no stranger to grabbing headlines with glitzy actor hirings such as Keanu Reeves, but will Rockstar's approach to marketing GTA 6 push it a step further?

"The most important takeaway - I'm not sure if I'd call it a lesson because this is our playbook as well - is that if you want to reach a certain critical mass, you do have to get out of just the core gaming bubble, something we did in the past as well," Nowakowski said. "For sure, GTA 6 went there.

"If the underlying question was if we're going to repeat or copy-paste their playbook: no, for sure not. Our games are different and they require a certain different approach - we just do things differently than they do. But in terms of the ultimate effect, in terms of breaking out to the mass market awareness: this is for sure something we consider pivotal to whatever we're going to do with our marketing campaigns in the future."

CDPR's Q3 financial results were positive. The company made less money than this time last year, but the "fresh momentum" - as Nowakowski put it - provided to The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 by the release of the Remastered edition of Witcher 3 and the Edgerunners anime series on Netflix, and associated game update, went a long way.

The Witcher 3 reached its highest concurrent player count on Steam as a result, and Cyberpunk 2077 reached its second highest concurrent player count, which represents serious staying power for both games so long after they were first released. And with Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past on track for 2027, and The Witcher 4 for 2028, the future is loaded.

The Voice newbie Riley Green is having a killer first season on NBC’s long-running singing competition, which is currently airing on the 2026 TV schedule. He easily won over the majority of the country music hopefuls during the Blind Auditions and has given the competitors excellent advice that they can continue to carry with them. But no competition is smooth sailing, and the “Don’t Mind If I Do” singer is revealing the toughest part of coaching.

With the Live Shows in full swing, the country hit maker has two of Season 30’s strongest contenders, Joe Henley and Ferryn & Brinkley, still on his team. As we move ever closer to the unveiling of the winning coach and star, Green, who can currently claim the title of being one of 2026’s Sexiest Men Alive, has struggled with having to send so many talented singers home. He told People why he’s having fun during the live performances:

I’m really excited that I’m not having to send people home. That was the toughest thing about what’s gone on so far. It was tough in the auditions because you hear these amazing stories that people have... and they’re taking off to come try to chase their dreams, and maybe they don’t get picked.

Nobody is ever really an overnight sensation, so The Voice’s superstar coaches absolutely understand what it’s like to chase your dreams and have setbacks along the way. I can’t imagine how agonizing it must be to know you have to send home some really talented singers. Whether you’re rookie Queen Latifah or veteran coach Adam Levine, cutting someone’s dream short never gets any easier. So, I get why Green is relieved to just sit back and enjoy the performances, and leave it up to the audience to decide who continues on and who gets cut.

In an interesting twist for Season 30, the Live Shows have replaced the Knockouts, which happen to be Levine’s least favorite part of the competition for a very similar reason. No The Voice coach wants to have to send home talented singers, and leaving it all in America’s hands takes the pressure off the coaches. The Marshals guest star also said this about his experienceon the show:

Worse than that is once you’ve worked with them and they are on your team and then having to send them home after that, I’m so sick of having to make those decisions. So I’m glad America can do it, and I’ll just try to help them along the way.

One of the best parts of the reality competition show is watching how the coaches really become fans of their own team members. Kelly Clarkson has expressed her commitment to continue collaborating with Team Kelly, and I’m sure other coaches feel just as dedicated to creating such a supportive atmosphere.

I wouldn’t be surprised to see Green touring or doing special performances with his Team Riley singers, especially considering how connected he sounds like he feels with all of them. Also, it would probably go a long way toward making him feel better for those departing contestants.

The Voice Season 30 continues to air on Mondays until December 14th, when a two-hour finale will reveal who is crowned the winner. You can also watch the next day with a Peacock subscription. And Season 31’s The Voice: Celebrity is already waiting in the wings with new host Keke Palmer.

#3546. The Steam Awards turn 10 with throwback categories and a Game of the Year Hall of Fame

Nominations for the 2026 Steam Awards are now open, and to mark the event's 10th anniversary, Valve has brought back some categories from years past and added a Hall of Fame.

You've got until 6pm UK (10am Pacific) on 30th November to nominate your favourite games of the year across 14 categories. Returning throwbacks include Just 5 More Minutes, Defies Description, and This is My Job Now, which recognises games that simulate mundane real-life jobs.

The new Hall of Fame category will appear when voting opens, and will let players choose their favourite from Steam's previous Game of the Year winners to crown the best game of the past decade.

Most categories are only open to games released on Steam since last year's Autumn Sale.

The exception is the Labo(u)r of Love award, which goes to older games that developers are still supporting with new content. Previous Labo(u)r of Love winners, including Warframe, Grand Theft Auto 5, Cyberpunk 2077, and Baldur's Gate 3, can't be nominated again.

Five finalists will be revealed in each category when voting opens alongside the Steam Winter Sale on 17th December. Voting closes at 10am Pacific on 2nd January, and the winners will be announced straight afterwards.

Nominating in at least one category also earns you the first level of Steam's Nomination Committee badge.

Earlier this month, Valve released a new Steam update that adds Steam Deck framerate data to a game's store page, giving potential buyers an indication of how well a game runs on the handheld.

CD Projekt made its Q3 2026 financial report today, and there's not a whole lot to see: The Witcher 3 remaster was a big hit, work on Cyberpunk 2 and The Witcher 4 is ticking along, and everyone really liked Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2.

Perhaps understandably, a number of questions in the subsequent investors call put the focus on Grand Theft Auto 6. While CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski didn't go too deep on the topic, he did say that the upcoming Witcher 4 will be comparable to GTA 6 in at least one way.

"Obviously, this is a call about us, not about Rockstar, but I do understand the connection here," Nowakowski said when asked if The Witcher 4 will represent a technological leap over its predecessor comparable to GTA 6. "Having said that, of course, I'm not going to make a deep dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course, we did look at the game. We did see the differences.

"Do we believe there's going to be a comparable leap between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4? I think so, yes. I mean, it's been 11 years. We are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game. So yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."

Well, sure. As Nowakowski said, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt was released 11 years ago, and it'll be two more years before The Witcher 4 comes out—assuming it's not delayed, which would make it a rarity among CD Projekt games. It will also be the same number of years between Witcher 3 and 4 as spanned GTA 5 and 6. In the world of technology, 13 years is a long time.

Hell, just the upgrade from the original Witcher 3 to the remastered version that dropped earlier this year is notable:

At the same time, Nowakowski said that while the GTA 6 launch was tremendously successful, CD Projekt Red doesn't intend to merely mimic Rockstar's approach when The Witcher 4 is ready to go: "Our games are different and the require a certain different approach, and we just do certain things differently than they do."

He also said that while the release of GTA 6 has had an impact on Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 sales on consoles, he doesn't expect it to have a "material impact" on the company's Q4 finances for one obvious reason.

"You do have to remember that a lot of our players are also PC-based," Nowakowski said. "GTA has not launched on PC. We have not seen any impact whatsoever on the PC sales on engagement." And, he added, "on the PS5 and Xbox, it's not like our sales came to zero."

Nowakowsi also said that GTA 6 hasn't changed CD Projekt's ambitions for The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2: If anything, it's "an inspiration in many ways for our developers." And he's not concerned about its success pushing up development budgets, because CD Projekt's games "are not budget-driven developments."

"I'm not saying that we don't care about the budgets. We do, and I'm pretty sure [Rockstar] did as well," Nowakowski said. "But you cannot make games like that having in mind, 'This is the fixed number of money I want to spend, and that's it. Otherwise, we're gone.'

"They are ambition-driven developments and money is important. The budgets are not indefinite. That's not what we're saying. But the philosophy is kind of like I said. And honestly, that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6's release. It has just always been like that."

Nowakowski's positive take on GTA 6 isn't too far off that of Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski, who said yesterday that he's suffering from "GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression," although he quickly clarified that CD Projekt is "doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor." #3544. Lords of the Fallen 2 delayed to April 2027, exact release date coming next month

Lords of the Fallen 2 will now launch in April 2027, and we'll find out exactly when next month.

The news came via a short post on X from CI Games founder and CEO Marek Tyminski. "Lords of the Fallen II: April 2027," he wrote. "Exact date in December."

That means the Soulslike sequel has slipped again. Back in June, CI Games pushed Lords of the Fallen 2 into a Q1 2027 release window, saying the extra time would let the team refine the game and keep it clear of "a highly competitive holiday period". That was a delay in itself, as when CI Games and Epic ended the game's PC exclusivity deal in May, it was still targeting a 2026 release.

Last month, CI Games secured a €28.6 million (around $32 million) loan to complete production and release Lords of the Fallen 2, as well as refinance its existing bank debt, according to a stock exchange filing. The loan matures on 31st August 2027, and, as reported at the time, CI Games will self-publish the game and expects to repay the loan through its sales.

Lords of the Fallen II: April 2027. Exact date in December. pic.twitter.com/yYaevDqaxe

Lords of the Fallen 2 is coming to PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store.

Following its announcement in 2025 and a look at gameplay during that year's The Game Awards, Lords of the Fallen 2 - which is technically the series' third game if we don't ignore the fact it was rebooted - had been steadily marching towards an unspecified 2026 launch. On PC, the plan was for it to be an Epic Games Store exclusive, but that's no longer happening after we learned CI Games - developer and sole owner of the IP - is now free from the multi-year exclusivity deal with Epic Games.

The sequel has also been at the centre of heated conversations following CI Games founder and CEO Marek Tyminski's comments regarding "political correctness" and "real player feedback". The studio also raised eyebrows recently by announcing more revealing armour sets for female characters in Lords of the Fallen 2, for instance, compared to its previous project.

Eurogamer gave the rebooted Lords of the Fallen two stars, calling it "a perfectly acceptable Soulslike that's often fun to play and offers the same satisfaction at overcoming adversity", but one let down by "Soulslike clichés and performance woes".

#3543. Selling Sunset’s Emma Hernan Reveals Where She Stands With Chrishell Stause

Emma Hernan is opening up about where her relationship stands with longtime friend-turned-foe and former Selling Sunset costar Chrishell Stause.

“We’re just in a place like — I haven’t heard, spoken [to her]. I mean like, we’re good in the sense where there’s never going to be a resolve there, you know what I mean?” Hernan, 34, said on the Monday, November 23, episode of the “Kaylor’s Crash Outs” podcast. “Sometimes the damage is done and when you hurt someone too bad, there’s just no coming back from that. … So that’s where I stand.”

Hernan clarified that she doesn’t “wish bad things” on Stause, 45, but wishes her “all the best.”

“There’s never going to be some moment where it’s back to where it was, you know,” she added. “But I know everyone’s curious about it and I think it’s fine to say, you know, it is one of those things where it is what it is. Everything happened. Everything unfolded the way it did. I wish her and — to be honest with you — everyone the best. But it’s not going to be something where I can’t really forget a lot of the stuff that I personally had to go through because of it, you know?”

Stause had been open about disliking Hernan’s romance with Blake Davis, accusing him of using a racial slur and mocking her then-partner G Flip’s pronouns. (Davis shut down Stause’s claims. Stause and G Flip have since split.)

Stause and Hernan subsequently had a falling out over Davis after season 10 production wrapped.

“I was there to help pick her up when they would break up and I would hear all of these horrible things — horrific things. You never want your friend to go back to that. What I can do is extract myself from a situation that is a toxic cycle,” Stause said during the reunion. “I can’t get an answer from you and you are lying about things that you are very clearly lying about. You are flaking on your friends and I really take that as a hit to the friendship.”

Hernan, however, defended her decision to be romantic with Davis.

“Who hasn’t dated a guy that your family or friends don’t agree with? I am human and I have feelings. Unfortunately, I made a connection with someone who isn’t the most likable person. There was a conversation that needed to be had,” she explained. “He doesn’t always behave, so that is why I take distance a lot.”

Hernan continued, “There have been multiple times where I haven’t spoken to him for two to three months at a time — like, completely ghost. At that moment, I feel like I will never speak to him again and then they will be able to see that I am with him. There’s a bond there. I am not saying he is the person I am going to marry. But I have had three boyfriends and he is the third.”

Hernan and Davis, meanwhile, have been on and off since their relationship began in 2024.

#3542. Wizards Goes To War With Magic: The Gathering Counterfeiters Over Printing ‘High-Quality, Realistic’ Proxies

Wizards of the Coast has filed a lawsuit alleging a Magic: The Gathering proxy cardâprinting business is actually a front for a counterfeit card operation. First reported by Aftermath, the MTG publisher’s lawsuit alleges that PrintMTG Enterprises not only offers buyers the opportunity to print cards that look “as realistic as possible,” but also uses hijacks website domains in an effort to sell their products.

At the heart of the alleged counterfeiting operation is a practice known as “proxying.” Sometimes players use what are known as “proxy cards,” or stand-ins for cards they don’t own or don’t want to damage by using in play. It’s a commonly accepted, sometimes even celebrated practice, as proxies can also feature cool, custom-made art. But proxies are not meant to look like real Magic cards, and that’s the crux of the issue with PrintMTG’s practice of printing cards that it calls proxies but that are designed to be indistinguishable from the real thing. “They intend that the people who encounter their product after the sale, including opponents, judges, retailers, and later purchasers, will mistake it for Wizardsâ genuine product,” Wizards writes in its suit.

According to Aftermath, Wizards’ lawsuit claims PrintMTG Enterprises operates out of a number of differently named websites, some of which have allegedly been obtained via domain hijacking. One website, KrakenOpus.com, was a luxury publishing operation whose website has now been turned into an independent MTG news site with links that direct users to a proxy printing website, proxyking.biz, which is currently down. The suit alleges that the business behind PrintMTG doesn’t just make counterfeit MTG cards, but fake PokÃ©mon cards and Lego minifigs as well.

Wizards of the Coast is seeking $28 million in damages.

Warning! The following contains spoilers for the 90 Day: Hunt For Love episode "The Boy Who Left His Mark." Stream the episode with an HBO Max subscription, and read at your own risk!

After their confrontation was shown in the previous episode, 90 Day: Hunt For Love finally showed Razvan Ciocoi's removal from the spinoff. I have mixed feelings about how it was handled, and questioning whether it was the best way for this to be shown to viewers.

For those unaware, Razvan was removed from 90 Day: Hunt For Love after he allegedly used a racial slur to refer to Jamal Menzies during their argument. Rather than show the incident, the 90 Day Fiancé show decided instead to flash the following text onscreen before moving on to the next day:

Razvan was asked to leave the retreat due to a code of conduct violation.

The scene then switched to Iris meeting up with the other 90 Day: Hunt For Love singles and explaining that he left. There was no discussion about what happened, and it was more to state that Iris was "back on the market" with her match gone. Had someone watching only learned of the incident from the 2026 TV schedule, they wouldn't have known what happened.

90 Day: Hunt For Love Has Me Wondering If Brittany Intentionally Sabotaged Michael's Love Life

I don't know all the context that went into this decision, but I can already see some problems with it. To start, I don't think avoiding what happened with Razvan is going to dissuade viewers out of the loop from looking up what happened. He was a prominent part of 90 Day: Hunt For Love up to this point, and I think his absence will be felt.

On the same token, there's a discrepancy on whether or not the event in question happened. Razvan has denied it was ever uttered, and if there was evidence to the contrary, TLC opted not to show it. Additionally, no one spoke about the incident beyond Razvan being gone, so it's still up in the air beyond TLC's statement.

I also would be willing to cut the franchise some slack, had it not just based an entire storyline in a previous spinoff on a racially insensitive remark by Shekinah Güven. 90 Day: The Last Resort dove deeply into her telling Thaís Ramone to "go back to her country," and even addressed it again at the tell-all special without her being present. So, I doubt the incident was a bridge too far by the show's standards, which makes me all the more curious why it was sidestepped.

The questions and drama will continue on 90 Day: Hunt For Love on TLC on Mondays at 8:00 p.m. ET. Despite this unfortunate moment, I'm still enjoying this season and wondering which couples will link up at the end of it all.

#3540. Missing Coach Travis Turner's Wife Has Been 'Bullied to Death,' Neighbor Says

The wife of missing high school football coach Travis Turner has seen her close-knit community turn against her amid her husband’s ongoing disappearance.

Leslie Caudill Turner has been “bullied to death,” one of her neighbors told the Daily Mail in a story published on Thursday, November 19. Another expressed fear that Leslie will “grieve herself” to death.

Travis and Leslie’s oldest son, Bailey, has convinced his mother to get off social media to avoid all of the hate.

“Because I would have been fighting everybody,” Leslie explained to the Daily Mail. “I guess that probably [isn’t] the best thing to do. So now I just stay to myself.”

Travis, 46, went missing on November 20, 2025, allegedly last seen by his family walking into the woods while carrying a rifle.

Shortly after he disappeared, Travis was charged with five counts of child pornography and five counts of using a computer to solicit a minor.

Bailey, 26, now works on the football coaching staff at Union High School in Big Stone Gap, Virginia, where his father led the program until his disappearance.

“He said he knew his dad would want him to stick with football,” Leslie said of her son’s role on the team. Travis and Leslie also share son Grayden, 21, and daughter Brynlee, 12.

Despite Bailey’s coaching job, Leslie explained that she doesn’t attend any of the games.

“Without Travis, I don’t keep up with anything,” she said. “I stay home, [go] to work and go home … I don’t want anybody talking to me about it.”

With the one-year anniversary of her husband’s disappearance come and gone, Leslie said the emotions are still raw.

“I just don’t have any closure, I cry every day,” she admitted.

Leslie added, “It’s like day one all over again. Every day that I’ve not been told that there’s a body found, I still have a little bit of hope. But I don’t think he’d be able to go an entire year without letting somebody know he’s okay.”

Ultimately, Leslie admitted she and her family are “already grieving like he’s dead.”

Leslie stopped short, however, of accepting the charges against her husband.

“I didn’t see anything. And I checked his phone before he left,” Leslie said. “It’s just it doesn’t do me any good because he’s not here. And I don’t get to fight him or cuss him. Nobody will ever get me to say anything bad about him.”

The search for Travis “remains active,” Virginia State Police exclusively told Us last month.

“There are no new developments to share at this time,” the VSP said on October 27. “Because Turner is considered a fugitive, the U.S. Marshals Service continues to lead the investigation. We understand the public’s concerns and frustrations as this case reaches the one-year mark.”

Sony has been crowing about Grand Theft Auto 6 setting a new record for concurrent PlayStation players, which isn't bad for a game that's currently only singleplayer. It isn't just beating the records set by the giants of multiplayer gaming back when they released, though. It's also eating their lunch right now.

Alinea Analytics reports that Call of Duty, Fortnite, and EA Sports FC 27 all saw their number of daily active users drop when GTA 6 released. "Call of Duty got it the worst of the three," Alinea's head of market analysis Rhys Elliott wrote, "dropping 42% from an average of 7.5M DAUs to 4.4M" according to the company's estimates.

Fortnite only lost 28% of its players, the firm claims, with an estimated five million of them choosing to buy groceries and fix the stairs instead of parachuting out of a bus over the weekend, and EA Sports FC 27 suffered a similar loss. "FC 27's DAUs dropped by about 27% when GTA 6 launched," according to Elliott, "from 5.9M to 4.3M."

But where player numbers for both of those games were trending back up four days after GTA 6's release, Call of Duty has struggled to win its players back, Elliott says: "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days. It's still down 41% from its baseline."

During that time Call of Duty had a Thanksgiving-themed event, while FC 27 had a Black Friday discount and in-game "Thunderstruck" promotion, and Fortnite's ongoing Treasure Hunters event is adding a bunch of One Piece stuff. If you're going up against a cultural juggernaut like GTA, I guess crossing over with something as massive as One Piece is the way to do it.

As Elliott concludes, this is only part one of the story. When Rockstar comes back for the second bite of this apple its rivals might have an even harder fight on their hands: "When the online component and PC port of GTA 6 hits (some time next year simultaneously, I'd imagine), then the bounce back will not be so obtainable."

Chris Columbus needed the job, but not badly enough to work with Chevy Chase.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Chris Columbus directed Home Alone, but he came remarkably close to spending Christmas with the Griswolds instead. Before that movie became a holiday staple, he was supposed to direct National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation. Then he met Chevy Chase, and Columbus' latest account makes his decision to walk away sound even gutsier than I realized.

OnWildmen, the podcast hosted by Dylan Sprouse and the director's son Brendan Columbus, he revisited the feud that's been part of Hollywood lore for years. I've heard the basic story before. What caught my attention was how badly he needed that movie, and how carefully he now talks about Chase. Columbus didn't dance around the history when the conversation turned to his early directing career:

I did not get along with Chevy Chase, and at this point famously now.

Columbus was coming off 1988's Heartbreak Hotel, which left him convinced his directing career might be over. He'd returned to Chicago and was staying with his in-laws when John Hughes called. The Christmas Vacation offer was supposed to get him back behind the camera, and he'd already started shooting second-unit footage.

The filmmaker has spoken harshly about Chase before. But this time, he said he's less interested in adding to the actor's bad press. Then he recalled how things reached the point where he called Hughes and quit:

I’ve reached a point where I disliked him so much, and had so much anger toward him, I think I’ve become mature enough, and I think he’s taken so much shit in the press for the past five years that I’m sort of like I’m tired — I don’t wanna say he’s a bad person. So, basically, because I didn’t get along with Chevy, I had to tell John Hughes. I said, ‘I can’t do the movie.' And I needed the movie desperately. I had already shot second unit on the movie for Christmas stuff in Chicago.

I appreciate that Columbus is making room for a little perspective here. He didn't suddenly declare the feud resolved or pretend the experience was pleasant. He just sounds tired of spending another interview beating up Chase. Fair enough. I'd be tired of telling that story, too, especially knowing it started with a job he desperately needed. But the Harry Potter franchise filmmaker continued:

Two weeks later, John sends me Home Alone. He says, ‘Okay, you can't direct Christmas Vacation. I got this other script.’

Jeremiah S. Chechik took over Christmas Vacation, and Home Alone arrived in theaters in 1990. I'm grateful both movies became Christmas classics, although it's amusing to imagine what Columbus might have done with Clark Griswold's disastrous holiday lighting display. Given those early meetings, I suspect he'd rather not imagine it at all.

Hearing Columbus discuss the timing makes it even stranger. A decision that could have ended his directing career led him to Kevin McCallister, Joe Pesci, and one of the most rewatchable Christmas movies around. I think I'm going to look at the opening credits a little differently this year. Excuse me while I go rewatch Home Alone for the 100th time with my Disney+ subscription.

Ryan graduated from Missouri State University with a BA in English/Creative Writing. An expert in all things horror, Ryan enjoys covering a wide variety of topics. He's also a lifelong comic book fan and an avid watcher of Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon.

How was life under Electronic Arts for BioWare? Not great, according to many former developers. But perhaps no quote has put the seemingly impossible situation the RPG powerhouse was put in more than one recently shared by Dragon Age executive producer Mark Darrah.

He left BioWare around 2021 and turned to making YouTube videos about life lessons for game development instead. He’s shared his thoughts on the many trials and tribulations BioWare faced both internally and in relation to its parent company’s insatiable lust for live-service recurrent revenue. But he framed the friction between studio and publisher especially starkly in a new interview with Pembridge TV (via VGC).

âSomeoneâI guess I wonât name them, just so I donât get them potentially in troubleâonce said that EA doesnât shoot you, it puts a gun on the table and then comes in every day and asks you if youâll shoot yourself,” Darrah said. “And they just keep coming in over and over, until eventually you just are like, ‘fine, todayâs the day, stop bugging me about it, Iâll do it.'”

The veteran developer said EA leadership never came in and made the bad decisions directly. Instead, they set broader objectives and laid out a list of options for meeting them that ranged from bad to worse. One famous example was the need to ship a game quickly because Star Wars: The Old Republic, the studio’s ambitious MMORPG, was falling behind. The Dragon Age team rushed into the breach and ended up delivering Dragon Age 2Â in under two years. The result was one of BioWare’s most poorly received RPGs.

âBasically, EA put a shotgun at the back of the studioâs head and said: ‘Fix this. Youâre about to put a massive hole in the revenue, in our financials. Fix it,'” Darrah said. He continued, “So the reality is, a lot of times EA can legitimately say, ‘we didnât make BioWare do this, they chose to do this.’ But if you dig underneath that statement, the reality is like: ‘Yeah, but you didnât reallyâ¦the options on the table were all terrible. We chose the least terrible of the options.'”

Instead of being a one-off, Dragon Age 2 proved a harbinger of worse troubles to come. While Mass Effect 3 and Dragon Age: Inquisition both blew audiences away, things eventually unraveled with a string of troubled development cycles on games including Mass Effect: Andromeda,Â Anthem and, most recently, Dragon Age: The Veilguard. Following its sale to Saudi Arabia over the summer, EA elected to cancel the upcoming Mass Effect: Universe and close the studio for good.

“I think it caught a lot of people by surprise because it was seen as sort of ‘well, they would never close BioWare,'” Darrah said. “But I think that every time a major studioâs closed, I think thatâs peopleâs reaction, is ‘they would never close X.'”

#3535. The Surprising History of the Royal Walkabout

“I have to be seen to be believed,” the late Queen Elizabeth II once said. And on Christmas Day, the royal family will be seen en masse during their annual walkabout on their way to services at St. Mary Magdalene Church on the Sandringham estate. For years, the holiday stroll, which features major and minor royals mingling with the public, has been a milestone event on the royal calendar.

But three controversial royals, the former Prince Andrew, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, almost certainly will not be there. While Andrew has disappeared into his new life at Marsh Farm in Norfolk, Harry and Meghan have continued the tradition of the walkabout, reportedly infuriating the palace with a planned meet-and-greet with a small group of well-wishers in Nottingham. Although no longer working members of the royal family, it seems the couple knows the value and the power of this famous tradition, whose origins are far more recent than many believe.

For centuries, commoners were lucky to get a glimpse of royals riding a horse on a march across the country or nodding from a carriage on the way to the opening of parliament. The first Buckingham Palace balcony appearance was not until 1851, when Prince Albert came upon the idea of Queen Victoria appearing to celebrate the Great Exhibition of London.

The leading figure behind the idea of making the monarchy more visible to the public was a surprising one: the dour, but savvy George V, who ascended the throne in 1910. “I may be uninspiring,” he admitted, “but I’m damned if I’m an alien.”

Queen Elizabeth II and Prince William waving from the balcony of Buckingham Palace during Trooping the Colour on June 16, 1990. Pictured: Prince Edward, Duchess Of York, Queen Mother, Princess Margaret, Queen Elizabeth II, Prince Philip, Prince William, The Grand Duchess Josephine Charlotte Of Luxembourg, Prince Harry, Prince Charles, Lord Frederick Windsor, Princess Diana and Lady Rose Windsor.

These royal appearances ramped up significantly during the first World War, when the royal family came under scrutiny for their German lineage. George visited everyday soldiers on the Front, and Queen Mary and her children spent hours visiting the wounded in hospitals.

“George took ‘getting out and about’ to new levels. He visited industrial areas and poor housing, went down a coal mine and went on a relentless round of opening hospitals and inspecting regiments,” royal news website Royal Central notes. “Queen Mary once retorted to a princess complaining about yet another hospital visit: ‘We are the royal family—and we love hospitals.’”

However, these events were still carefully curated, with a distance maintained between the royal family and those they were visiting. It was not until 1939, that the first unofficial walkabout occurred, when King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (better known as the Queen Mother) went to tour Canada on a goodwill tour in the midst of the looming war. In May, the couple laid a wreath at Ottawa National War Memorial while an estimated 10,000 veterans looked on.

Overcome with emotion, the royal couple decided to go into the crowd to speak with onlookers. A CBC radio journalist watching the scene could hardly have sounded more in awe. “They all look most happy, most excited,” the reporter said. “One had the hand of the queen in one hand and the hand of the king in another. A delighted expression.”

George and Elizabeth were equally touched, and continued these meet-and-greets throughout the tour. “I lost my heart to Canada and to Canadians, and my feelings have not changed with the passage of time,” the Queen Mother recalled.

Known for her effusive personality and warmth, the Queen Mother became a pro at speaking with everyday subjects. During World War II, George and Elizabeth were praised for going among the people in bombed out areas devastated by the Blitz, listening to their woes and offering encouragement and strength.

Queen Elizabeth II on walkabout in Launceston, Tasmania, during her tour of Australia, 1970.

But it was not until Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip toured Australia and New Zealand in 1970 that the modern walkabout was truly introduced into the British royal calendar. There are different origin stories about how the modern walkabout came to be. One version asserts that it was a spontaneous decision of the Queen to walk to her next stop in order to chat, shake hands and accept flowers from schoolchildren in New Zealand.

Others say that first walk was the brainchild of the modernizing Australian courtier William Heseltine, known as the “mastermind behind the monarchy.” A firm believer in making the family seem more approachable and normal, he was also behind the 1969 Royal Family documentary. But if that project proved to be controversial, the walkabout (a term coined as a result of the tour) was a smash hit.

According to Kitty Kelley, the first royal walkabout did not occur in London until 1972, during the celebration of Elizabeth and Philip’s 25th wedding anniversary. “People were agog; their sovereign had never been known to speak to ordinary people,” Kelley writes in The Royals. “This was the first royal walkabout London had ever seen, and flag-waving Britons cheered as the Queen, the Duke of Edinburgh, Prince Charles, and Princess Anne melted into the crowd, greeting people and trying to make the royal family appear less remote.”

While the Queen reportedly enjoyed the intimacy of the walkabout, not every royal family member was quite as thrilled. “At nineteen years old suddenly being dropped in the middle of the street, suddenly being told to pick someone and talk to them,” Princess Anne said. “Fun? No, I don’t think so. A challenge.”

Queen Elizabeth II visits the Town Hall in Sydney with Emmet McDermott, Lord Mayor of Sydney, during her tour of Australia, May 1970.

Soon, the walkabout was a major part of every royal’s schedule, and family members had to learn how to do them—like it or not. “I learnt the way a monkey learns—by watching its parents,” King Charles once said.

During international tours, the walkabouts made a packed schedule even more tiring, but Queen Elizabeth II never faltered. “On a tour of Canada, visiting Saskatchewan, the Canadian minister Alvin Hamilton was concerned that the Queen had been on her feet all day and had not even requested a ‘health break,’” Karen Dolby writes in The Wicked Wit of Queen Elizabeth II. “Her private secretary breezily replied that the Minister for Northern Affairs and National Resources need not worry, ‘Her Majesty is trained for eight hours.’ It’s impossible not to wonder about the training sessions.”

She also leaned upon her sense of humor when meeting folks of all different stripes. “On a walkabout in Scotland, a helpful observer commented that she looked just like the Queen, to which she quickly replied, ‘How reassuring,’” Dolby notes.

According to Dolby, the Queen also developed a system to communicate with her staff while talking with the public. If things were going well, she held her handbag in the crook of her left arm. If she wanted someone to relieve her so she could move on, the handbag was dropped to her side.

But the person who truly transformed the modern walkabout was Princess Diana, much to her husband Prince Charles’s chagrin. “Charles was smart enough to see what a stunning political asset Diana had become—but he was also deeply disturbed by all the adoration coming his young wife’s way,” Tina Brown writes in The Diana Chronicles.

From the start it was clear the young Princess had a connection with everyday people unlike any other royal. During a walkabout while touring Wales in 1981, Charles joked, “I seem to do nothing but collect flowers these days, I know my role.”

As Dianamania swept the world, the Princess became more and more comfortable with connecting with her often-rabid fans. Far from a stiff gloved handshake, she would clasp hands gloveless, hug well-wishers, kneel to speak with children. Frustrated that Diana constantly pulled focus, Charles delivered pithy one-liners with a forced smile. At one walkabout, the crowd openly groaned when they realized Charles was coming to their side, not Diana. “It’s not fair is it?” Charles quipped to the crowd. “You’d better ask for your money back.”

But despite Charles’s jealousy, he could not deny the impact Diana had during these walkabouts. “Everyone was really buoyed up to see her and she was making an effort to go along and speak to people and people appreciated the effort she put into meeting them,” one person she spoke with remembered. “I know it was her job but she gave that little bit extra to people that made her different and stand out.”

“She made people happy,” he noted. “It’s a rare gift.”

Catherine, Princess of Wales, has followed in her mother-in-law’s footsteps as a walkabout all-star. According to historian Robert Jobson, Catherine was initially scared during the walkabout, offering up the stiff refrain, “Thank you so much. We are so delighted to be here,” over and over. But she quickly acclimated and has become known for her chatty and warm ways. “There’s a real art to walkabouts,” she has said. “Everybody teases me in the family that I spend far too long chatting. I still have to learn a little bit more, and to pick up a few more tips, I suppose.”

In fact, it has become a sport for the press to catch Prince William subtly attempting to move Catherine along, often eventually giving up. During the Christmas Day walkabout in 2024, she was the last royal to leave the receiving line, quipping “I think I’ve lost my family!”

According to royal author Robert Hardman, King Charles can also be unusually chatty. No one quite wants to go up and go, ‘Sir, can you get a move on?’ he says. “Instead, Queen Camilla will nudge him in the small of his back with the corner of her handbag.”

But the predilection is one Camilla shares as well. On a walkabout in Wrexham, an irritated Charles was overheard telling an aide “Can we try to get [Camilla] back again? Please? We need to go! I was trying to wait for her, but she goes on!”

Prince Harry and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, attend University of the South Pacific on October 24, 2018 in Suva, Fiji.

Learning the art of the walkabout—what to say, what not to say—is a lesson every royal must figure out, often on the job. When Meghan Markle married Prince Harry in 2018, she admitted her ignorance. “I never saw pictures or videos of a walkabout,” she claimed.

And with the advent of cell phones, the job has become much more difficult. “I’m glad that I’m not starting now because at least you had people to talk to. Now you don’t really. Phones are bad enough, but the iPads—you can’t even see their heads,” Princess Anne said.

And these engagements can occasionally go south. In 2018, the Duchess of Sussex was rushed out of a market in Fiji after the walkabout got out of hand. There are also the occasional overzealous fans, including recently when a woman attempted to kiss Prince William on the cheek. And who can forget the supremely uncomfortable walkabout at Windsor after the Queen’s death in 2022, when a warring William, Catherine, Harry and Meghan greeted public mourners. It was, Catherine reportedly said, “one of the hardest things she’d ever had to do.”

Walkabouts are also a logistical headache for royal protection officers. “You are always aware of who is in the crowd,” former royal bodyguard Simon Morgan explained to Hello! “That is one of the positives of our royal family, they always want to go and meet people and as a protection officer, you have to accept what their wishes are. The current trend of hugs, high fives and selfies, that’s going to continue, so the protection officer’s job is really brought to the front then, because the protection officer is constantly looking for what could go wrong, you are constantly working things through your mind for the ‘what if, what if, what if.’

But the walkabout shows no sign of disappearing anytime soon. And come Christmas Day, there will be cheers, hugs, and an enormous amount of quick, polite chats about the weather that citizens who wait and brave the winter cold will never forget.

It’s kind of hard to believe that Vanna White has been co-hosting Wheel of Fortune for nearly 45 years as of the 2026 television schedule. For thousands of episodes, White has been turning the iconic letter on the show, but her beginning was as humble as you would expect. In a recent appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, White told the story of her audition, why she was chosen by legendary producer Merv Griffin, and even what her first puzzle was (and the first letter she turned).

Of the audition process, White explained:

Merv Griffin, God bless him. He chose me…. [There were] over 200 girls. And I said to him, ‘Why did you choose me?’ He said, ‘You turn the letters better than anyone else.’

I mean, yeah, fair enough, right? Though White’s role on the show has grown a lot over the years, far beyond only turning (now touching) the letters (and working hard for her salary). In those early days, that was the job. If you’re going to get the gig, you better be elegant when you are flipping those lit-up boxes around! No one can argue with Griffin’s logic, and almost five incredible decades later, it's clear he couldn’t have made a better choice.

Speaking of turning letters, Fallon follows up White’s story about getting the job on Wheel by asking her if she remembers her first puzzle, and despite thousands of puzzles since, she does:

It was ‘General Hospital,’ and my first letter was a T.

According to White, she’d wanted to be a TV star since she first saw her “uncle,” actor Christopher George, in an episode of his show The Rat Patrol in the mid ‘60s. George, it should be noted, was not a biological uncle, but was a close friend of her mother’s. On her first day filming, however, she was still quite nervous (and was even worried it wouldn't work out in the early days), telling Fallon:

I was so nervous. Oh my gosh. My teeth were [chattering], I couldn’t even talk. I was like, ‘Oh my gosh, is this really happening?’

Famously, that wasn't the first time appearing on a game show. Two years before getting the job, she appeared as a contestant on The Price Is Right. Fallon and White talked about that appearance, which, sadly, ended without her making it on stage with Bob Barker, as she was never closest to the price of the item while on contestants' row.

White's first episode of Wheel aired on December 13, 1982, which means we’re just a couple of weeks away from her 44th anniversary. Pat Sajak was her co-host, of course, and the duo would work together for the next 42 years before Sajak retired from the show in 2024. She continues to co-host with Ryan Seacrest and has shown no signs of slowing down as she approaches 70 years old.

Wheel of Fortune airs daily across the country and can be streamed with a Peacock subscription.

#3532. Man Killed Wife and 2 Kids in Murder-Suicide That’s Left Family ‘Heartbroken’

Authorities in New Mexico said a man fatally shot his wife and their two young children before taking his own life in an apparent murder-suicide.

Police responded to a home in Las Cruces, New Mexico, on Thursday, November 19, around 10 a.m. after a relative reported that she couldn’t get in touch with anyone who lived at the home.

Once officers got to the residence, they discovered the bodies of four family members who had all suffered gunshot wounds.

Following a preliminary investigation, authorities determined that Marcus Reyes Sr. fatally shot his wife, Alayna Reyes, their son, Marcus Jr., and their daughter, Anastacia.

After he killed his family members, Marcus Sr., 28, seemingly died by suicide.

It’s not currently clear whether authorities believe Marcus Sr. had a motive in the killings or if the family had a history of domestic violence issues.

In light of the tragedy, Alayna’s aunt, Kim Vallejos, launched a GoFundMe to financially support Alayna’s mother and the kids’ grandmother.

“I’m raising funds to help my sister with family support and relief fund, immediate family needs, and other expenses arising from the tragedy after the deaths of her daughter Alayna, grandchildren Marcus and Anastacia,” Vallejos wrote on the fundraiser’s page. “This unimaginable loss has left us heartbroken. They were so loved and will be missed.”

Vallejos concluded, “If you are not in a position to donate, sharing this fundraiser and keeping our family in your thoughts and prayers would mean more than you know.”

The fundraiser has earned $25,496 out of its $28K goal as of time of publication.

In addition to the fundraising information, Vallejos shared several photos of the victims. One photo captured Alayna, 28, and Marcus Jr., 8, spending quality time together in a park, while another featured the mother and Anastacia, 6, during a day at the beach. Another photo showed the siblings donning large grins as they enjoyed ice cream.

The murder-suicide has left the family’s neighbors in shock, with some of those who lived nearby speaking to ABC 7 about the killings.

Neighbor Erika Sorensen said that the suburban community where the family lived is “a very calm, quiet area.” She added, “It’s very unnerving that it’s just right there.”

“Nothing like this has ever happened. It’s heartbreaking. It’s so sad,” neighbor Katie Albright told the outlet.

Albright added that “everybody’s talking about how we’re processing it with our kids, and how we’re processing it with each other.”

“And, you know, looking for ways that we can hopefully support the family,” she said.

If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org.

#3531. Cheeky Malware Linked To Popular Gacha Game Cracks City Security

East Asia--and particularly Japan--has been suffering a rash of cybersecurity incidents as of late, affecting everything from major banks and cellphone service providers to city governments and small businesses. Gaming has been one of many areas targeted: between arcade games on Sega's network going offline, 11 million Capcom IDs being compromised, and a high-schooler hacking Bandai-Namco, some major publishers have been suffering a string of embarrassments.

One recent incident involved the PC launcher for the popular gacha action shooter NIKKE: Goddess of Victory, where malicious code would install a trojan called k2f that would compromise an individual's PC, taking screenshots, logging inputs, and installing/executing programs. Unfortunately for one Japanese municipality, someone's gacha habits may have lead to a much bigger incident.

Iwamizawa is a city of about 75,000 located in Hokkaido, Japan's northernmost island. It's not a place that makes a lot of news, but it recently went viral on the Japanese-speaking side of social media. As reported by Automaton, the city issued a notice that an IT sub-sub-contractor handling the city's fixed asset records suffered a security breach--specifically, a k2f hijack. Observers soon surmised that the most likely source of k2f would be someone playing a certain sexy gacha game on a work PC.

The subcontractor in question, IT services company GIS Hokkaido, would then confirm to Japanese tech news site ITMedia that, yes, NIKKE's compromised PC launcher was the source of the problem. When asked if an employee or subcontractor had launched the game on a work PC, GIS politely replied that "they would prefer not to comment."

Moral of the story? While there's nothing wrong with playing a suggestive gacha game on your own time, you probably shouldn't do it on the clock, and definitely not on a company PC, lest you become internet meme fodder.

#3530. Kate Middleton Wore Matching Amethyst Necklace and Earrings for Her First Engagement in India

The Princess of Wales touched down in India this Monday for a whirlwind three-day visit to the country with her husband, Prince William.

The couple visited Mumbai for the sixth Earthshot Prize Summit, which took place on Tuesday. It marked the Waleses’ first joint overseas visit since Catherine’s cancer diagnosis.

The busy schedule of engagements kicked off with a game of gully cricket—an informal version of the game played on the street. For the occasion, the Princess of Wales struck a balance between polished and casual, opting for crisp white Alexander McQueen trousers, paired with a white top layered under a pistachio blazer by Veronica Beard.

The Princess of Wales debuted a pistachio blazer by Veronica Beard for the outing

The finishing touch? A matching set of green amethyst earrings and a drop necklace from one of Catherine’s favorite jewelry labels, Kiki McDonough. Catherine has at least 20 pairs of earrings from the jeweler, ranging from the blue topaz drops she wore to Royal Ascot to the green tourmaline, green amethyst and diamond earrings set in gold, designed specially for her to mark Princess Charlotte’s birth.

The apple green amethysts, which she wore in Mumbai, are among the lesser-seen designs in her collection but proved the perfect accessory for this first engagement.

While in Mumbai, the prince’s program focused on The Earthshot Prize and its mission to accelerate solutions to the world’s most pressing environmental challenges. The princess joined the prince for a number of engagements during the visit.

The Prince and Princess of Wales in Mumbai on Monday

During their time in Mumbai, the prince and princess also celebrated several of the deep cultural connections between the United Kingdom and India: cricket, fashion, and cinema.

Beginning with an engagement focused on the uniquely Indian passion of gully cricket andconcluding with a visit to the heart of Mumbai’s film industry, their royal highnessescelebrated the creativity, talent, and cultural influence that continue to shape modern India andstrengthen ties between the two countries.

The highlight of the visit was the Earthshot Prize ceremony on Tuesday, November 17. Five Earthshot leaders were given 1 million euros (about $1.1 million USD) to accelerate the impact of their innovative solutions. Mumbai made perfect sense as the host city; India is home to more Earthshot Prize winners and finalists than any other country.

The Princess of Wales looked elegant in a lime green blazer layered over an all-white ensemble

Since founding the prize in 2020, Prince William has attended all of the awards ceremonies: in London, Boston, Singapore, Cape Town, and Rio de Janeiro. Catherine joined the prince in London in 2021 and again in Boston the following year, but has missed recent editions in the further corners of the globe. This was partly due to the princess’s restricted work schedule while she underwent treatment for cancer and spent time in recovery.

It marked a return to the country for Prince William and Kate, who carried out a state visit in April 2016. The week-long tour saw the then Duke and Duchess of Cambridge explore Mumbai, New Delhi, Assam, and Bhutan, racking up a total of 22 engagements that saw them try their hand at cricket, meet Bollywood stars and royalty, and champion charitable causes close to their hearts.

It was one of four overseas trips taken by the couple that year. Although William and Kate still travel, it is with far less frequency as the couple prioritizes a stable family life. Their last major overseas tour was to the Caribbean in 2022.

#3529. GTA 6: Don’t Finish Chapter 2 Before Doing These Things

GTA 6's first chapter is a lengthy prologue that gets you up to speed on the gameplay, the characters, and the storyline. But once you've cleared the final mission and you start Chapter 2, that's when the game really begins. This is where the protagonists Jason and Lucia cement their decision to go full Bonnie and Clyde, and since this chapter unfolds at a faster pace, you'll want to keep an eye out for a few missable items, people, and missions before you hit the point of no return that leads directly into Chapter 3.

Which mission ends Chapter 2 in GTA 6?

Appropriately, Chapter 2 in GTA 6 ends with the mission Checking Out after you reach the Move to Vice City point on your map, as Jason and Lucia will leave their current residence behind as they embark on a new journey to Vice City. To get there, you'll need to complete the following missions:

  • What's in the Bag?
  • Ambulance Chaser
  • Just Moved In
  • Girls' Trip
  • Moses
  • Daily Driver
  • Slam Dunk
  • Breakfast Run
  • Coffee Break
  • Afternoon Delight
  • Checking Out

Optional missions

There's also a bunch of optional missions you can engage in, in case you want to score some more gear, unlockables, and cash before your Vice City trip:

  • Check Out McKittrick Farm
  • Collect Chemicals for Kyle
  • Hit Avery Pawn
  • Hit Kingpin Bowling
  • Impounded Vehicle
  • Pick Up a Gun
  • Thrillbillies
  • Twist Wrist, Smash, Grab
  • Veteran Hunted (Jason only)

Pay your room rent as quickly as possible

One of your primary goals in Chapter 2 should be settling your debt with the motel manager Linda, as the more you delay paying her, the higher your checkout fee will be. If you purchased a necklace for Lucia in Chapter 1, Linda will hold it as collateral until the debt is settled, so reclaiming that sentimental piece of jewelry should be a priority.

Talk to Wyman

Chatting to Wyman and helping him out with his truck will also earn you an invite for a bit of off-roading fun with two of the missions: Thrillbillies and Twist, Wrist, Smash, and Grab.

Find missing people

While you don't have to tackle the Gellhorn’s Missing Tourist challenge as part of GTA 6's missing people questline during Chapter 2, it is recommended that you get this out of the way early. Starting this quest from Chapter 3 will be more challenging--for spoiler-specific reasons--and you can find those people of interest by checking nearby bulletin boards, posts, and notices.

Play some pool

Before you rob Frankie's Delights, go shoot a few rounds of pool to check off another task in your quest to be the biggest pool shark around.

Grab some collectibles

Several collectibles can be found in the Chapter 2 motel, so before you say goodbye to that location for good, grab 'em and sell 'em to help you reach a 100% completion rate in the game.

Collectible cards

  • Bryson Powers: On top of the washing machine in the motel laundry room
  • Vicki: In the motel reception bathroom, on the floor underneath the toilet
  • Victor Maravella: Check the fridge in the motel cafeteria

Magazines

  • Help Me Help You Help Me: On the motel reception desk
  • Wizard Wang: In the motel cafeteria, next to the radio

For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

And I was able to gauge the impact of my involvement, which gave me the confidence I needed to launch Rhode. Without imagining it would become so big. No matter how much you dream of reaching as many people as possible, nothing is ever guaranteed.”

The documentary has been making tons of headlines.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The buzziest film on the 2026 movie schedule has to be You Can See Everything, and it just hit a major milestone by crossing the $100 million mark at the box office. For a movie that was made for a reported $7 million, it’s certainly one of the most successful A24 releases ever, but the Elizabeth Holmes documentary is nowhere close to the top-grossing documentary of all time, worldwide. That record belongs to the King of Pop himself for the posthumously released Michael Jackson: This Is It from 2009. How does it stack up to other documentaries? Well, it depends on how you count things.

Anyway you count, in terms of worldwide gross, This Is It sits at the top of the list, with almost $268 million, according to Box Office Mojo. Second on the list is Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour, which made $261 million worldwide, and most of it ($180 million) in the United States. Both far outpace Fahrenheit 9/11, which is third on the list and the first non-music documentary. The Michael Moore-directed movie about the lead-up to the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq was a box office sensation from the moment it was released.

You Can See Everything wasn’t quite the rocket ship that Fahrenheit 9/11 was out of the box, but it did a ton of steady business for weeks, finally topping the weekend box office in its third week of release. Now, after its release in the United Kingdom, the Nathan Fielder/Lance Oppenheim-directed documentary has joined rarefied air as a documentary hitting that milestone. The $100 million mark slots You Can See Everyone into 7th worldwide.

Nature documentaries litter the top ten, with the IMAX-exclusive Everest, (filmed during the disastrous season on the mountain in 1996) coming in fourth all time, Earth coming in at #6 on the list (Penguins is 5th), and Oceans is 9th. The other slots in the top ten are both music-related: Justin Bieber: Never Say Never (8th) and One Direction: This Is Us (10th).

Here are the top ten-grossing documentaries of all time (worldwide), along with their gross, according to Box Office Mojo:

That means the only two non-music and non-nature documentaries in the top ten are Fahrenheit 9/11 and You Can See Everything. It also means that You Can See Everything won’t be catching up to Michael Jackson. I don’t expect You Can See Everything to improve significantly at the worldwide box office. Elizabeth Holmes may be fascinating and infamous here, but Jackson was a massive star in every corner of the globe. In fact, domestically, This Is It actually trails You Can See Everything by almost $20 million.

It’s the domestic numbers that really tell you the story of just how buzzy the film is, as it ranks 3rd all time at U.S. box offices, behind Fahrenheit 9/11 and The Eras Tour. It also has a very good chance of separating itself from the pack as the first documentary nominated for Best Picture at the Oscars, something not even March of the Penguins did. Who knows, maybe it will be competing against this year's Michael in that category.

You Can See Everything is now available on video-on-demand with a Prime subscription or other VOD formats.
